title: Sequence-mix throughput synthesis log
content:
Purpose:
This notebook-style log captures an exploratory series of microbenchmarks aimed at understanding how mixed sequence-length workloads interact with kernel selection policies (FlashAttention variants, paged attention paths, and fused operator groups) in our serving runtime. The goal is to synthesize realistic mixed loads and find robust heuristics that avoid tail-latency regressions while preserving throughput and GPU utilization.

Background / motivation:
- Production traffic at multiple customers shows heavy variance in sequence length; 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512).
- Our kernel selector currently picks kernels deterministically based on sequence length, batch size, and model family. Observed cases where small fluctuations in batch composition flip the selected kernel and cause 3-8x latency spikes for a small fraction of requests.
- Hypothesis: stochastic or smoothed selection (with hysteresis) could reduce jitter by preferring stable kernels across short windows, at modest throughput cost.

Experiment design:
1) Workload synthesis:
   - Build synthetic request traces that mimic production mix: short:medium:long ratios 6:3:1, with Poisson arrival (lambda tuned to saturate target GPU occupancy).
   - Two variants: uniform sequence distribution and bursty windows where long sequences arrive in bursts of 1-2s.

2) Kernel families evaluated:
   - FlashAttention v2 (fused kernels, single-shot)
   - Paged-attention (flashpaged-style prefetch + tiny fused ops)
   - Fused-op chain (explicit fused matmul + custom attention pass)

3) Selection policies:
   - Deterministic: current prod rule (length threshold mapping).
   - Stochastic-sample: choose best-mean kernel with probability proportional to expected throughput given current batch histogram (seeded RNG to allow repeatability).
   - Windowed-hysteresis: stick to chosen kernel for N batches or T ms unless throughput drops by >X%.

4) Metrics collected:
   - p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end request), per-token generation latency, kernel execution time (device-side), GPU SM utilization, memory bandwidth, batch formation delays, scheduler queue length.
   - Failure cases: kernel fallbacks, OOMs, kernel launch failures, CQ stall events.

Test harness and config:
- Cluster: 1x A100-80GB (driver + CUDA 12.1), Linux 5.15, runtime branch: perf/seq-mix-smoke (PR 678).
- Model: 7B LLM (dense) compiled with our optimized kernels; sequence length cap 2048.
- Batching: dynamic batching up to 32 sequences; time-budget=10ms.
- Repeats: 10 runs per config, each run 300s after warmup.

Observations (high level):
- Deterministic selection produces lowest median latency under steady-state uniform mix but exhibits a p99 tail spike when a long-sequence burst shifts the batch histogram and triggers a kernel switch mid-workload. The spike magnitude correlated with number of in-flight KV-cache entries requiring a new kernel path.
- Stochastic-sample reduced the frequency of giant tail events by ~55% at the cost of ~6% throughput reduction (measured as tokens/sec) under uniform mixes. The randomness helped avoid synchronized switches across worker threads.
- Windowed-hysteresis (T=200ms, N=3 batches) provided a better tradeoff: tail event frequency down ~70% and throughput loss ~2-3%. Shortening hysteresis to 50ms removed benefit; longer than 500ms introduced throughput regression for heavy long-seq phases.
- Paged-attention path performed best for mixed workloads when the long-seq fraction was >=15% due to incremental prefetch amortization, but suffered additional batch formation latency for short-heavy mixes.
- Fused-op chain had the best single-kernel throughput for long sequences but poor small-batch latency because of kernel launch overhead and less effective continuous batching.

Numeric snapshot (representative):
- Uniform mix (6:3:1), occupancy target ~75%:
  - Deterministic: p50 12ms, p95 42ms, p99 210ms, tokens/sec 120k
  - Stochastic-sample: p50 13ms, p95 46ms, p99 95ms, tokens/sec 112.8k
  - Windowed-hysteresis: p50 12.5ms, p95 44ms, p99 63ms, tokens/sec 117k

- Bursty long-window (bursts 1.5s every 10s):
  - Deterministic: p99 spikes up to 1.2s during bursts; repeated kernel fallbacks logged.
  - Windowed-hysteresis: p99 ~140ms, far fewer fallbacks.

Root-cause notes and traces reviewed:
- Kernel handoff requires reinitializing scratchpad and KV-cache state for fused-ops → this is expensive when many inflight small batches are waiting. The scheduler currently allows kernel switches at batch-formation boundaries, which may overlap with inflight micro-batches causing serialization.
- FlashAttention path shows higher sensitivity to batch-size variance: for batch-size<4 launch overhead dominates and aggregate SM occupancy is low.
- Paged-attention benefits from prefetched pages when upcoming sequences tend to be long; accuracy of prefetch predictor matters.

Actionable changes to prototype / next steps:
1) Implement windowed-hysteresis in kernel selector (configurable T and N) and add metrics to track "selection churn" per worker. WIP branch: perf/selector-hysteresis.
2) Add a simple moving-average estimate of incoming sequence length distribution (exp decay alpha=0.2) and use it as an input to the selection policy.
3) Improve the kernel handoff path: allow a lightweight "mini-warmup" for scratchpad allocation that can be executed asynchronously for next kernel to avoid blocking current micro-batches. Prototype PR queued: /runtime#682.
4) Add a fallback mitigation: if a kernel switch would cause >X% increase in expected p95 given current backlog, delay the switch until backlog drains below threshold.
5) Expand synthetic trace set: include client-side real-user traces (anon) from customer A (consent confirmed) to validate behavior in production-like burst patterns.

Open questions / discussion items:
- How to set hysteresis parameters adaptively per-model family? We saw different optima for 7B vs 13B. Suggestation: autosuggest T and N from offline traces.
- Is stochastic selection acceptable for enterprise SLAs where determinism is preferred? Maybe expose it as an opt-in runtime toggle for Dedicated customers.
- Can paged-attention prefetch predictor be trained online from short-run statistics to adapt to burstiness?

Appendix: observed logs snippets (trimmed) 
[2024-11-09T15:12:34Z] worker-03 SELECT kernel=flash-v2 batch_hist="S:18 M:6 L:2"
[2024-11-09T15:12:34Z] worker-03 LAUNCH kernel=flash-v2 seq_avg=78 batch_size=26 exec_ms=8
[2024-11-09T15:12:36Z] worker-03 SELECT kernel=paginated-1 batch_hist="S:4 M:3 L:25"
[2024-11-09T15:12:36Z] worker-03 KERFH: scratch_reinit_ms=92 inflight_microbatches=7
[2024-11-09T15:12:36Z] worker-03 observed-tail-latency p99=1.2s (burst)

Notes to self / heuristics to try:
- Try T = 2x mean-kernel-exec-ms; ensure min N=2 to avoid flip-flopping on single microbatch.
- If stochastic-sample used, cap randomness so worst-case kernel is not chosen >20% time.

References and related docs:
- perf/attention-selection-design (Confluence)
- GitHub: runtime/pull/678 (bench harness), runtime/pull/682 (handoff mini-warmup)
- JIRA: INF-3421 (kernel selection jitter)

Summary (one-liner):
Windowed-hysteresis + light moving-average of sequence mix offers the best immediate payoff: big reduction in tail events with minimal throughput cost. Follow-up work should harden the kernel-handoff path and test adaptive parameter selection across model families.

Action items (who/when):
- Ravi: land hysteresis prototype and smoke tests by 2024-11-20.
- Evy: run expanded synthetic trace battery and post results to PR 678 by 2024-11-18.
- Marco: prototype async mini-warmup flow and open PR for review by 2024-11-22.

End of log.
